findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical sublinear boundary-search solution. Connectivity makes black-row and black-column projections contiguous, the known pixel anchors the monotone halves, and four constant-space binary searches recover the exclusive rectangle bounds. The implementation is clear and expert-quality, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 302 and its Python string-row image plus known-pixel contract. The Reference preserves connectedness, the strict better-than-O(mn) requirement, both source examples without explanations, all eight constraints, and an accessible text equivalent of the source illustration.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064360345. It and the app-local source have identical dimensions, monotone row and column predicates, binary-search transitions, anchored search ranges, exclusive boundaries, and area formula; the app's string rows are the sole representation adaptation.

The former 256 by 256 tier violated the source's 100 by 100 ceiling. Legal 16 by 16, 40 by 40, and 100 by 100 tiers now retain a centered connected 3 by 3 component and span 39.0625x in cell count. The current source passes at -0.01 relative exponent and 0.95x largest ratio; a correct full-image boundary scan passes all outputs but fails only scaling at +0.34.

The Approach now defines dimensions m and n before the manifest bound, derives projection contiguity from connected paths, explains both predicate transitions and exclusive limits, and distinguishes singleton and edge-touching components.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against authenticated source evidence, preserving both examples without explanations, all eight constraints, the connected-region and runtime requirements, and the informational equivalent of the sole source image.

coverage: Both authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact image facts, known-black coordinates, and rectangle areas; string rows preserve the documented app adapter.
The invented horizontal row is now a trial rather than a source sample, and the formerly hidden asymmetric white-border case is visible.
The 1 by 1 singleton covers both minimum dimensions, while one-row and one-column components exercise the maximum width and height of 100.
Top-left, bottom-right, full-image, interior-singleton, and white-border cases exercise every inclusive and exclusive search boundary and every legal known-pixel position class.
Irregular, asymmetric, L-shaped, and cross-shaped components preserve four-neighbor connectivity while covering internal white cells and distinct row and column projections.

An independent bounding-box and connectivity oracle verified all 14 authored results and all three benchmark results; the protected source also matched it for every known black anchor across 14,324 connected binary images up to 4 by 4, totaling 127,150 anchored inputs.
All 14 correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 16 by 16, 40 by 40, and 100 by 100 scaling images remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
